newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ansett sees big savings - executive.
newsitem.headline: Ansett sees big savings - executive.

text.p: Ansett Australia aviation policy manager James Kimpton said on Monday the airline hopes to achieve substantial savings from the tough cost-cutting measures it has put in place.
"In terms of getting back to short-term profitability we are very much looking at our costs," Kimpton told an aviation industry conference in Canberra.

"We are looking at our costs both in the sense of looking at everything which we procure, everything on which we spend money and making sure that we are only consuming on those things which we really need and we're doing it at the lowest cost.
Kimpton said the airline would continue to focus on developing its existing international operations.
"My understanding from my colleagues it that the focus will continue on developing operations in the areas we are currently serving," he said.
Ansett hoped to increase services to Japan and Hong Kong to daily flights from the current frequency of five a services week.
It was also seeking to boost its other international services to five a week. Ansett flies to Seoul, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta and Bali.
Ansett executive chairman Ken Cowley in August ordered managers to cut A$150 million from Ansett's annual A$3 billion cost base.
